mainTopic: Does a husband's sin with his wife's relative forbid his wife, and what is the ברייתא's "light prohibition"?
overview: The גמרא explains why a man who unknowingly sinned with his wife's sister does not lose his wife. Even a deliberate sin does not forbid her by תורה law, so the רבנן made no decree. A ברייתא learns this from the word ״אותה״: only the wife's own relations forbid her. Without that word, a קל וחומר might have suggested otherwise. The ברייתא records a debate between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי over whether בית שמאי and בית הלל argued about the wife's sister or the mother-in-law. רבי יוסי reasons that a husband forbids his wife to all men, while she forbids him only to her relatives, and he builds a קל וחומר from this. ריש לקיש gives רבי יהודה's source from ״באש ישרפו אותו ואתהן״, but שמואל rules against רבי יהודה, and רב יהודה acts on that ruling in a real case. Finally, the גמרא tries to identify the ברייתא's "light prohibition": a remarried divorcée, a יבמה, and a סוטה are each proposed and challenged, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A wife's sister is different
steps.stepSummary: With a wife's sister, even a deliberate act does not forbid the wife on a תורה level, so the רבנן made no decree for an unknowing act.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a wife's sister: even when it is done on purpose, the wife is not forbidden by תורה law, so when it is done by mistake the רבנן did not make a decree about her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a distinction it started just before. It explains why the wife stays permitted when her husband unknowingly sinned with her sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is that the רבנן add decrees only where the deliberate act is already forbidden by the תורה. Here, even a deliberate act with the wife's sister does not forbid the wife מדאורייתא. So there is no reason to forbid her when the act was unknowing (שוגג).

phrases.aramaic: אֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה, דִּבְמֵזִיד לָא אֲסִירָא מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
phrases.english: A wife's sister, where even on purpose she [the wife] is not forbidden by Torah law,
by mistake, the Sages did not decree about her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה, דִּבְמֵזִיד לָא אֲסִירָא מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a distinction begun just before this section.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think an unknowing act with the wife's sister should forbid the wife by rabbinic decree.
steps.terutzMaskana: No decree applies, because even a deliberate act does not forbid her מדאורייתא.

steps.title: Where do we learn she is not forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a wife's sister does not forbid the wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that she is not forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for what it just said. This question sets up the next step, which brings the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 rested entirely on the claim that the wife is not forbidden מדאורייתא. The גמרא now wants to see where the תורה teaches that.

keyTerms.meaning: and from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that she is not forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the claim in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that relations with the wife's sister do not forbid the wife.

steps.title: The word ״אותה״ — only her own act forbids her
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from ״אותה״ that only the wife's own relations with another man forbid her, not her sister's relations with the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: "her." "Her" means her own lying with another man forbids her, but her sister's lying does not forbid her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that reads the word ״אותה״ ("her") in the סוטה passage as limiting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word "her" narrows the rule. A wife becomes forbidden to her husband only through her own act (שכיבתה). Her sister's relations with the husband do not make her forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: her (a limiting word in the verse)

phrases.english: As it is taught: "her"
"her": her own lying forbids her,
but her sister's lying does not forbid her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The limiting word ״אותה״ teaches that only the wife's own relations forbid her.

steps.title: Why the verse was needed: a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that without the verse, a קל וחומר would have suggested the wife does become forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: For one might have thought: isn't it logical? If where he has relations under a light prohibition the one who causes the prohibition becomes forbidden, then where he has relations under a severe prohibition, isn't it logical that the one who causes the prohibition becomes forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows why the word ״אותה״ was necessary: without it, a logical argument would have led to the opposite conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a hypothetical challenge, a קל וחומר. If even a "light" forbidden act makes someone forbidden, a "severe" one should all the more so. The verse comes to block that conclusion. Starting at step 14, the גמרא tries to identify what the "light" case is.

keyTerms.meaning: isn't it logical? (opening of a קל וחומר)
the one who causes the prohibition

steps.confusionAlert: This קל וחומר is NOT the conclusion. It is the mistaken line of thinking that the word ״אותה״ comes to reject.

phrases.english: For one might have thought: is it not logical?

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁבָּא עַל אִיסּוּר קַל —
phrases.english: If in a place where he has relations under a light prohibition,
the one who causes the prohibition is forbidden,
then in a place where he has relations under a severe prohibition,
is it not logical that the one who causes the prohibition is forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the derivation in step 3 was needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from a light prohibition to a severe one would make the wife forbidden, so a verse is needed to teach otherwise.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the dispute is about the wife's sister
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says everyone agrees that relations with the mother-in-law disqualify the wife; בית שמאי and בית הלל argue only about the wife's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about a man who had relations with his mother-in-law; there, he disqualified his wife. What did they argue about? A man who had relations with his wife's sister: בית שמאי say he disqualified her, and בית הלל say he did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a תנאים debate. Here רבי יהודה gives his version of what בית שמאי and בית הלל argued about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, the mother-in-law case is agreed upon: the wife becomes disqualified. The argument is only about the wife's sister. In that case בית הלל say she is not disqualified, which fits the derivation from ״אותה״.

keyTerms.meaning: he disqualified (his wife from staying with him)
the schools of שמאי and הלל

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree

phrases.aramaic: בְּבָא עַל חֲמוֹתוֹ שֶׁפָּסַל אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ,
phrases.english: about one who had relations with his mother-in-law, that he disqualified his wife.
About what did they disagree?
About one who had relations with his wife's sister:
Beit Shammai say: he disqualified [her],
and Beit Hillel say: he did not disqualify [her].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא continues with a תנאים debate about where בית שמאי and בית הלל disagree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mother-in-law: the wife is disqualified by agreement. Wife's sister: disputed, and בית הלל say she is not disqualified.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the dispute is about the mother-in-law
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי reverses it: everyone agrees the wife's sister does not disqualify the wife; the argument is about the mother-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about a man who had relations with his wife's sister; there, he did not disqualify his wife. What did they argue about? A man who had relations with his mother-in-law: בית שמאי say he disqualified her, and בית הלל say he did not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives the opposite version of the debate between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, the wife's sister case is agreed upon: the wife stays permitted. The argument is about the mother-in-law. So both תנאים agree that, according to בית הלל, the wife's sister does not disqualify the wife.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי simply swap which case is agreed and which is disputed. Keep a chart: for רבי יהודה the mother-in-law case is agreed; for רבי יוסי the sister case is agreed.
steps.whatToRemember: Either way, בית הלל hold that relations with the wife's sister do not disqualify the wife.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree

phrases.aramaic: בְּבָא עַל אֲחוֹת אִשְׁתּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא פָּסַל אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ,
phrases.english: about one who had relations with his wife's sister, that he did not disqualify his wife.
About what did they disagree?
About one who had relations with his mother-in-law:
Beit Shammai say: he disqualified [her],
and Beit Hillel say: he did not disqualify [her].

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite version of the dispute from רבי יהודה's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wife's sister: the wife is not disqualified by agreement. Mother-in-law: disputed.

steps.title: Why his prohibition on her is bigger than hers on him
steps.stepSummary: קידושין make the wife forbidden to every man in the world, but make the husband forbidden only to her relatives, so his prohibition on her is the larger one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because at first he is permitted to all the women in the world, and she is permitted to all the men in the world. Once he betrothed her, he forbade her and she forbade him. The prohibition by which he forbade her is greater than the prohibition by which she forbade him: he forbade her to all the men in the world, and she forbade him only to her relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a reason by comparing the two prohibitions that קידושין create. According to this reading, it explains רבי יוסי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before קידושין, both are free to marry anyone. Afterward, she is closed off to every other man, while he is closed off only to her relatives. This comparison is the base for the קל וחומר in the next step: the 'bigger' prohibition is the one on her, and the 'smaller' one is the one on him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This comparison of "his prohibition" and "her prohibition" is the foundation of רבי יוסי's קל וחומר in the next step, which shows that a husband's unwitting sin with her relative does not forbid his wife.

phrases.english: Because at first,
he is permitted to all the women in the world,
and she is permitted to all the men in the world.
Once he betrothed her, he forbade her, and she forbade him.
Greater is the prohibition by which he forbade her
than the prohibition by which she forbade him.
For he forbade her to all the men in the world,
and she forbade him only to her relatives.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁבַּתְּחִלָּה, הוּא מוּתָּר בְּכׇל הַנָּשִׁים שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the view just stated, by comparing the two prohibitions created by קידושין.
steps.raayaObject: That the husband's sin with his wife's relative does not make his wife forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logical comparison: the husband's prohibition on the wife (all men) is far greater than her prohibition on him (only her relatives).

steps.title: A קל וחומר that an unwitting husband is not forbidden to his wife
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי argues: if the wife, whose קידושין forbid her to all men, is not forbidden to her husband after an unwitting sin, then the husband, who is forbidden only to her relatives, is surely not forbidden to her after an unwitting sin with her sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this a simple logical argument? He made her forbidden to every man in the world, and still, if she sinned by mistake with a man forbidden to her, she does not become forbidden to the one permitted to her, her husband. She made him forbidden only to her relatives. So if he sinned by mistake with a woman forbidden to him, isn't it logical that he does not become forbidden to the one permitted to him, his wife?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי uses the idea from step 7, that the wife's prohibition is the bigger one, to build a קל וחומר. The point is that an unwitting sin by the husband with his wife's sister does not forbid his wife to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stronger case is the wife: her קידושין forbid her to the whole world, yet an unwitting sin does not cut her off from her husband. The weaker case is the husband, who is forbidden only to her relatives. So he surely is not cut off from his wife after an unwitting sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it logical? This opens a קל וחומר argument.
The one forbidden to her (any man other than her husband).
The one permitted to her (her husband).
Her female relatives (such as her sister or mother).

phrases.english: Isn't it a logical argument:
If he, who made her forbidden
phrases.notes: "He" is the husband: his קידושין made her forbidden to everyone else.

phrases.english: to all men in the world,
and she sinned by mistake with one forbidden to her —
she is not forbidden to the one permitted to her,
then she, who made him forbidden
only to her relatives,
if he sinned by mistake with one forbidden to him —

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא נֶאֱסַר (לוֹ) בַּמּוּתָּר לוֹ?!
phrases.english: isn't it logical that he is not forbidden to the one permitted to him?!
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The meaning is the same either way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the comparison in step 7, that her prohibition is bigger than his, as the base of a קל וחומר.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי's claim that the husband's sin with his wife's sister does not forbid the wife.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the wife's unwitting sin, which does not forbid her to her husband.

steps.title: The logic covers a mistaken sin, so what about a deliberate one?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא notes that the קל וחומר only covers a שוגג, and asks for the source for a מזיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: This logical argument works for one who sinned by mistake. For one who sinned on purpose, where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא admits that its קל וחומר only proves the case of a mistaken sin. It asks where we learn the case of a deliberate sin, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר was built on the wife's unwitting sin, so it can only teach about an unwitting sin by the husband. A wife who sins on purpose does become forbidden to her husband, so the comparison breaks down for a deliberate sin. Another source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it? A request for a source.

phrases.english: And this logical argument is for one who sinned by mistake.
For one who sinned on purpose, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the קל וחומר of step 8 to an unwitting sin and asks about a deliberate one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that even a deliberate sin with the wife's sister does not forbid the wife.

steps.title: The word ״אותה״ covers even a deliberate sin
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק's word ״אותה״ teaches that only the wife's own relations forbid her, not the husband's relations with her sister, even if he sinned on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says ״אותה״, "her": her own relations make her forbidden, but relations with her sister do not make her forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from the word ״אותה״, which covers even a deliberate sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same reading of ״אותה״ seen in step 3. Here it has a new job: it fills the gap the קל וחומר could not cover, the case of a deliberate sin.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches. This introduces a verse as the source.

phrases.english: The verse states: "Her,"
"her": her own relations make her forbidden,
but relations with her sister do not make her forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9's question about a deliberate sin.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ״אותה״ limits the prohibition to the wife's own relations, so even a deliberate sin with her sister does not forbid her.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוסי, a husband's sin with his wife's sister never forbids his wife to him. A mistaken sin is covered by a קל וחומר, and a deliberate sin is covered by the word ״אותה״.

steps.title: ריש לקיש gives the source for רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that רבי יהודה learns from ״באש ישרפו אותו ואתהן״: the whole household cannot be burned, so the word ״ואתהן״ must teach that both women become forbidden to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said in the name of ריש לקיש: What is the reason of רבי יהודה? Because it is written: "They shall burn him and them in fire." Would the whole household be burned?! If this cannot be about burning, apply it to being forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי יהודה from step 5, who holds that relations with the mother-in-law forbid the wife, and gives his source in a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to say that both the wife and her mother are burned, but the innocent wife did nothing wrong. Since the word ״ואתהן״ cannot really mean she is burned, it is used to teach something else: both women become forbidden to the man.

keyTerms.meaning: If it cannot apply to this topic. A rule for moving a verse's lesson to another topic.
A prohibition. Here it means that she is forbidden to him.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up רבי יהודה, the תנא whose opinion is being explained here, with רב יהודה, the אמורא in the next steps who quotes שמואל.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said that Reish Lakish said:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?
As it is written: "They shall burn him and them in fire,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:14. "Them" means the woman and her mother.

phrases.english: Would the entire household be burned?!
If it does not apply to burning,
apply it to being forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יוסי's reasoning back to רבי יהודה's view and supplies his source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a man who has relations with his mother-in-law becomes forbidden to his wife as well, learned from ״ואתהן״.

steps.title: שמואל: the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה, so relations with the mother-in-law do not forbid the wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is not like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling: we do not follow רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה, a man who sins with his mother-in-law does not become forbidden to his wife. The sin itself is still a serious sin.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה does not follow (this opinion).

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halakha is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the opinion whose source was just explained.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, relations with the mother-in-law do not forbid the wife to her husband.

steps.title: רב יהודה flogs a sinner but does not forbid his wife
steps.stepSummary: A man sinned with his mother-in-law. רב יהודה had him flogged, and told him that only שמואל's ruling stopped him from forbidding his wife to him forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man sinned with his mother-in-law. רב יהודה had him brought and flogged. He said to him: If not for the fact that שמואל said the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה, I would make her forbidden to you forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows שמואל's ruling applied in a real case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה punished the man with lashes for his sin. He did not forbid the wife, because he followed שמואל's ruling. His words show that he took רבי יהודה's view seriously, but held back because of the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A permanent prohibition, literally "a prohibition of the world" (forever).

steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה follows שמואל: a husband's sin with his wife's mother is punished, but his wife does not become forbidden to him.

phrases.english: A certain man committed a transgression with his mother-in-law.
Rav Yehuda had him brought and had him flogged.
He said to him:
If not for the fact that Shmuel said
the halakha is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda —
I would make her forbidden to you permanently.
phrases.notes: "Her" is the man's wife, not his mother-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows שמואל's ruling from step 12 applied in practice by רב יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: That the practical הלכה follows שמואל against רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה's ruling in a real case, where he flogged the sinner but did not forbid his wife.

steps.title: Which case is the 'light prohibition'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means when it speaks of an 'איסור קל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'light prohibition'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's קל וחומר and asks which case it calls a 'light prohibition.' This question sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר starts from a light case where the one who causes the prohibition also becomes forbidden. It then argues that this should certainly be true in a stricter case. To judge whether the argument works, we first need to know what the light case is.

keyTerms.meaning: A light prohibition, the starting case of the קל וחומר

phrases.english: What is the 'light prohibition'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the story of רב יהודה to explain a phrase in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case is the ברייתא's 'light prohibition' where the one who causes the prohibition also becomes forbidden?

steps.title: רב חסדא: remarrying a divorcée after she married another man
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the light prohibition is a man who remarries his divorcée after she married someone else, where each man's relations forbid her to the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is one who remarries his divorcée after she married another man. The גמרא explains: if this man (the second husband) has relations with her, he forbids her to that man (the first husband). If the other man (the first husband) has relations with her, he forbids her to this man (the second husband).
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא names the case of מחזיר גרושתו משנשאת. He shows that in this case, whoever causes her to become forbidden also becomes forbidden himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second husband's relations make her forbidden to the first husband. If the first husband then takes her back and has relations with her, she becomes forbidden to the second husband too. So the prohibition works in both directions, which fits the ברייתא's idea that the one who forbids is himself forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who takes back his divorced wife
He made her forbidden to him

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
One who remarries his divorcée after she married another man.
If this one (the second husband) has relations with her,
he has forbidden her to that one (the first husband).
If the other one (the first husband) has relations with her,
he has forbidden her to this one (the second husband).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַחְזִיר גְּרוּשָׁתוֹ מִשֶּׁנִּשֵּׂאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The light prohibition is remarrying one's divorcée after she married another man, where each man's relations forbid her to the other.

steps.title: That prohibition is not light at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב חסדא's answer: remarrying a divorcée is strict in three ways, so it cannot be the 'light' starting point.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about one who remarries his divorcée after she married another man? That case is different, because the body becomes defiled, her prohibition applies to most people, and her prohibition is permanent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא argues that this case is too strict to be called a 'light prohibition.' So it cannot be the starting point of the קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three strict features are listed. The פסוק calls her 'defiled' (נטמא הגוף), her prohibition applies broadly to most people, and it never ends. A wife's sister, by contrast, becomes permitted after the wife dies, so the קל וחומר would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What about...?' A way of showing that the starting case is different, so it cannot prove anything

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying this case is unimportant. It is saying the opposite: it is too strict to count as the 'light' side of the קל וחומר.

phrases.english: What about one who remarries his divorcée after she married another man?
It is different, because the body is defiled,
and her prohibition applies to the majority,
and her prohibition is a permanent prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב חסדא's identification from step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects remarrying a divorcée as the 'light prohibition' of the קל וחומר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case has three strict features (defilement, broad application, permanence), so it cannot serve as the light side of a קל וחומר.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the light prohibition is a יבמה
steps.stepSummary: After rejecting רב חסדא, the גמרא brings ריש לקיש, who says the light prohibition is a יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, ריש לקיש said: It is a יבמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רב חסדא's answer and gives ריש לקיש's answer instead: the case is a יבמה, a widow waiting for יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition involving a יבמה is a lighter one, so it fits the 'light' side of the קל וחומר. The next step asks for more detail about how the case works.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow of a childless man, waiting for her husband's brother

phrases.english: Rather, Reish Lakish said:
It is a yevama.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that was rejected in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The light prohibition is the case of a יבמה.

steps.title: With whom was the יבמה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which man had relations with the יבמה in ריש לקיש's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: A יבמה with whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a detail of ריש לקיש's case: who was the man with the יבמה? This sets up the options that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'forbidder becomes forbidden' idea works differently depending on whether she was with a stranger or with the יבם. So the גמרא has to spell out the case before it can test it.

phrases.english: A yevama with whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for details about ריש לקיש's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the יבמה's relations were with another man or with the יבם.

steps.title: First option: with another man, following רב המנונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests she was with another man, which would follow רב המנונא's ruling that such a שומרת יבם becomes forbidden to her יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say she was with another man, that would follow רב המנונא, as רב המנונא said: A שומרת יבם who had forbidden relations is forbidden to her יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out the first option: she was with a different man. It brings רב המנונא to explain how that would fit. This is a proposal the גמרא is about to examine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יבם's tie to her forbids her to every other man. Yet according to רב המנונא, if she is with another man, she becomes forbidden to the יבם himself. That would show 'the one who forbids becomes forbidden' in a light case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a proposal that is about to be tested)
A widow waiting for her יבם

phrases.english: If you say: with another man,
and this follows Rav Hamnuna,
as Rav Hamnuna said:
A widow waiting for her yavam who had forbidden relations
is forbidden to her yavam —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first possible answer to step 18's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Possibly she was with another man, following רב המנונא's ruling that she then becomes forbidden to her יבם.

steps.title: The יבמה case is too strict to be the light starting point
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first reading of ריש לקיש's case, a יבמה who was with another man. That case is strict, so it cannot serve as the light base.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a יבמה? Her body was defiled, and she is already forbidden to most people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 19. It says the יבמה case has strict features, so it cannot be the 'light' case we need.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19, a שומרת יבם who was with another man becomes forbidden to her יבם. The גמרא now points out that this case is strict in two ways: her body itself was defiled, and she is already forbidden to almost every man. A light case is supposed to have no such extra strictness, so this one fails.

keyTerms.meaning: the body became defiled, meaning the act itself made her forbidden
her prohibition applies to most people

phrases.english: What about a יבמה,
since the body was defiled,
and her prohibition applies to most people.
phrases.notes: While she waits for the יבם, she may not marry anyone else, so she is already forbidden to nearly every man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of ריש לקיש given in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: ריש לקיש's יבמה case, read as a יבמה who was with another man
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case has its own strict features (defilement of the body, and she is already forbidden to most men), so it is not light.

steps.title: A new reading: a יבמה among the brothers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads ריש לקיש's case as a יבמה among the brothers. One brother does מאמר, which forbids her to the others. Then another brother has relations with her, which forbids her to the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means a יבמה in relation to the brothers. If this brother did מאמר with her, he forbade her to that one. If the other brother then had relations with her, he forbade her to this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a different way to understand ריש לקיש's יבמה. In this version, the second man is one of the brothers, not an outsider.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מאמר is a kind of betrothal done by the יבם, so it ties her to that brother. Then a second brother has relations with her, and now she is forbidden to the first brother. Here each brother's act forbids her to the other, and the case does not involve the strictness of an outsider.

keyTerms.meaning: a betrothal-like act a יבם does with the יבמה before יבום

phrases.english: Rather, a יבמה in relation to the brothers.
If this one did מאמר with her,
he forbade her to that one.
If the other one had relations with her,
he forbade her to this one.
phrases.notes: Now "this one" is the first brother, the one who did the מאמר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 20 rejects the outsider case, this offers a new case definition for ריש לקיש.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The light case is a יבמה among the brothers, where מאמר by one brother and relations by another forbid her to each other.

steps.title: Why mention relations? מאמר should forbid her too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the case needs the second brother to have relations with her. A second מאמר should also forbid her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why specifically say that the second brother had relations with her? Even if he only did מאמר with her, it should forbid her too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading from step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We need a case where the act of relations is what causes the prohibition. If a second מאמר would have the same effect, then the relations are not the real cause, and the case does not fit what we are looking for.

phrases.english: Why specifically that the second had relations with her?
Even if he also did מאמר with her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case defined in step 21.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a second מאמר would also forbid her, then the relations are not what causes the prohibition.

steps.title: Following רבן גמליאל, a second מאמר does nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case follows רבן גמליאל, who holds that a מאמר after another מאמר has no effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. The case follows רבן גמליאל, who said: there is no מאמר after a מאמר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends step 21 against the challenge of step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבן גמליאל, once one brother has done מאמר, a second brother's מאמר does nothing. So only the second brother's relations could forbid her, and the case works.

keyTerms.meaning: there is no מאמר after a מאמר

phrases.english: This is not difficult,
it follows רבן גמליאל, who said:
There is no מאמר after a מאמר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the case to a specific תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A second מאמר would forbid her, so the relations are not what matters.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבן גמליאל, a second מאמר has no effect, so only relations forbid her.

steps.title: But a גט or חליצה would forbid her too
steps.stepSummary: The answer still fails. Even a גט or חליצה from the second brother would forbid her to the first, so the relations are not the cause.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still: even if he gave her a גט, and even if he did חליצה with her, she would be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the brothers-יבמה reading after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if we accept רבן גמליאל's view, a גט or חליצה from the second brother would still forbid her to the first. So the prohibition does not come from the relations, and this case cannot be our light base.

keyTerms.meaning: did חליצה, the ceremony that releases a יבמה

phrases.english: But still, even if he gave her a גט,
and even if he did חליצה with her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the attack of step 22 with acts that רבן גמליאל's rule does not cover.
steps.kashyaTarget: The brothers-יבמה case, even as defended by רבן גמליאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט or חליצה alone forbids her, so the relations are not the cause of the prohibition.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ends the יבמה line completely and opens the way for רבי יוחנן's new suggestion.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says the light case is a סוטה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the light prohibition is a סוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן said: a סוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: After the יבמה cases fail, the גמרא brings a new candidate from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוטה is a wife who was warned by her husband and then secluded herself with another man. רבי יוחנן says this is the light case where relations forbid her to someone else. The next steps work out exactly how.

keyTerms.meaning: a wife suspected of adultery after her husband warned her and she secluded herself with another man

phrases.english: Rather, רבי יוחנן said:
A סוטה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected יבמה approach with a new case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The light prohibition is a סוטה.

steps.title: Forbidden to whom?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: to whom does the סוטה become forbidden in this case?
steps.simpleTranslation: A סוטה, forbidden to whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for clarification about רבי יוחנן's case. This sets up the options that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two men involved, the husband and the other man. The גמרא needs to know whose relations forbid her to whom.

phrases.english: A סוטה, to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of רבי יוחנן's case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which man's relations forbid her to which other man.

steps.title: First option: the husband forbids her to the other man
steps.stepSummary: The first suggestion: the husband has relations with her, and this forbids her to the man she secluded herself with.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we say she is forbidden through the husband: the husband had relations with her, and that forbade her to the other man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out a first way to read the סוטה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, the husband's relations are what forbid her to the other man. The word אילימא tells us this is only a trial suggestion, and the גמרא will test it next.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say, a trial suggestion
the other man she was suspected with

phrases.english: If we say, to the husband:
The husband had relations with her,
and he forbade her to the other man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first answer to the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The husband's relations forbid her to the other man.

steps.title: But a גט, or refusing to give her the water, would forbid her too
steps.stepSummary: Why does the case need relations? She would be forbidden to the other man even if the husband only gave her a גט, or said he will not make her drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why specifically say he had relations with her? Even if he gave her a גט, and even if he said 'I will not make her drink', she would be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the husband reading from step 27, using the same kind of attack as in step 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She becomes forbidden to the other man even without the husband's relations, through a גט or through his refusal to give her the water. So the relations are not the cause, and this reading does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: I will not make her drink the סוטה water

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוחנן's answer has been rejected. Only the first reading of it (the husband forbidding her to the other man) is under attack here.

phrases.english: Why specifically that he had relations with her?
Even if he gave her a גט,
and even if he said, 'I will not make her drink'!
phrases.notes: He means he won't have her drink the special water used to test a סוטה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading suggested in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the husband's relations forbid the סוטה to the other man
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גט, or refusing to give her the water, forbids her just as much, so the relations are not the cause.

steps.title: A new reading: the סוטה with the other man
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the earlier reading. It suggests instead that the case is a סוטה whose relations with the other man (the בועל) forbid her to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is a סוטה who had relations with the other man.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier explanation failed, so the גמרא offers a new one. The relations that count are between the סוטה and the other man, and they make her forbidden to her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 28 the problem was that relations were not needed to forbid her to the other man, since a גט alone would do it. So the גמרא flips the case around. Now the relations themselves are what forbid her, this time to her own husband.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the גמרא is dropping the previous idea and offering a new one.
The man who had relations with her. Here it means the other man, not the husband.
A married woman suspected of being unfaithful to her husband.

phrases.english: Rather, a סוטה with the other man
phrases.notes: He means her relations with the other man, which make her forbidden to her husband from then on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reading from step 27, which was rejected in step 28, with a new way of understanding the סוטה case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'light prohibition' is a סוטה whose relations with the other man forbid her to her husband.

steps.title: That is not light, it is the severe prohibition of a married woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reading. A married woman having relations with another man is the severe prohibition of אשת איש, so it cannot be called a light prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this a light prohibition? It is a severe prohibition, namely a married woman!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reading it just offered. It says this case cannot be the 'light prohibition' that רבי יוחנן was describing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole search is for a case of a light prohibition (איסור קל). A married woman with another man is אשת איש, one of the most serious prohibitions in the תורה. So this reading contradicts the very thing it was meant to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: A light prohibition, meaning a less severe one.
A married woman. Relations with her are one of the most severe prohibitions.

phrases.english: Is this a light prohibition?
It is a severe prohibition,
since this is the prohibition of a married woman!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי אִיסּוּר קַל הוּא? אִיסּוּר חָמוּר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects the new reading offered in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in step 29 that the 'light prohibition' is a סוטה with the other man.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That case is the prohibition of אשת איש, which is severe. It cannot serve as an example of a light prohibition.
